## ② . Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises No. 16

The Ministry of Finance issued Interpretation of Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises No. 16 (" Interpretation No. 16 ") on December 13, 2022. According to Explanation No. 16:

A. For a single transaction that is not a business merger and does not affect either accounting profit or taxable income (or deductible loss) when the transaction occurs, and the assets and liabilities initially recognized result in the equivalent amount of taxable temporary difference and deductible temporary difference, the deferred income tax liabilities and deferred income tax assets are no longer exempted from the initial recognized deferred income tax liabilities.  For the  taxable  temporary differences and deductible temporary differences arising from the initial recognition of assets and liabilities  in  such  transactions,  the  Company  recognizes  the  corresponding  deferred  income  tax liabilities and deferred income tax assets respectively at the time of the transaction, which will be implemented as of January 1, 2023.

B. As the issuer of financial instruments classified as equity instruments, if the dividend payouts recognized on such financial instruments are deducted before corporate income tax in accordance with the provisions of tax policies, when the Company recognizes dividends payable, the income tax impact of such dividends shall be recorded into current profit and loss for the transactions or events that have generated profit and loss before the distribution of profits; If the distributed profit is derived from the transaction or event previously recognized in the owners' equity, the income tax impact of the dividend shall be included in the owners' equity item and shall be implemented as of the date of publication.

C. For modifying the terms and conditions of the share payment Agreement settled in cash to make it  settled in equity (including if the modification occurs after the end of the waiting period), the Company shall, on the amendment date, calculate the payment in equity settled in equity based on the fair value on the date of the equity instrument granted, and include the services acquired into the capital reserve. At the same time, it shall terminate the recognition of the shares settled in cash to pay the liabilities recognized on the amendment date, and the difference between the two shall be recorded into the current profit and loss, which shall be implemented as of the date of publication.

According to the test, except the above companies, the recoverable amount of the asset group of the acquired companies was higher than the book value, and the goodwill of the asset group showed no sign of impairment.

c. Information about the asset group or asset group combination where goodwill is located The value of the company's book goodwill is not formed by mergers and acquisitions under the same control, and the asset group or asset group combination involved in goodwill is consistent with the asset group or asset group combination determined during the goodwill impairment test on the purchase date and in previous years.

d. Goodwill impairment testing process, key parameters (such as forecast period growth rate, stable period growth rate, profit rate, discount rate, forecast period, etc., when predicting the present value of future cash flows) and the recognition method of goodwill impairment loss At the end of each year, the Company conducts impairment tests on the above consolidated goodwill in accordance with relevant provisions of the Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises No. 8 - Asset Impairment. At the end of the year, the Company will separate the subsidiaries listed in the above table as an asset group and allocate all the corresponding goodwill. The above asset group is determined in accordance with the asset group or combination of asset groups determined at the purchase date of each corresponding acquisition project and at the goodwill impairment test of previous years.

The recoverable amount of the Company's assets group including goodwill shall be determined as the higher of the present value of the estimated future cash flow or the fair value minus the disposal cost. The company estimates the cash flow in the next 5 years and the perpetual period according to the financial budget approved by the management. The pre-tax discount rate used to calculate the recoverable amount is 12%. The above financial estimates are prepared by management based on a comprehensive analysis of historical operating conditions, business plans, macroeconomic environment, industry conditions and market prospects, as well as projected realizable project revenues in the years after 2023.In this year, according to the difference between the book value of the asset group containing goodwill and the recoverable amount of the asset group containing goodwill, 1,632,426.72 yuan of goodwill impairment reserve is determined for Shanxi Hongyang Seagull Waste Electrical and Electronic Products Recycling Co., Ltd., and 301,502.05 yuan of goodwill impairment reserve for Inner Mongolia Xinchuang Resource Regeneration Co., Ltd. The total amount of goodwill impairment accrued for the year was RMB 1,933,928.77.

After testing, SHU POWDERS LIMITED, GEM (Jiangsu) Cobalt Co., Ltd., GEM (Hubei) New Energy Materials Co., Ltd., Zhejiang Meiqingbang Engineering Services Co., Ltd., GEM (Chenzhou) Solid Waste Treatment Co., Ltd., PT.QMB NEW ENERGY MATERIALS, GEM (Zhejiang) Power Battery Recycling Co., Ltd., etc. The recoverable amount of the asset group of the acquired company is higher than the book value, and there is no sign of impairment of the goodwill of the asset group.

## 3. Disposal of subsidiaries

Disposal of subsidiaries in the current period: None.

4. Changes in the scope of consolidation for other reasons
- (1) Merge range increase
3. ① In January 2022, Jingmen Huineng Labor Service Co., Ltd. was established by second-tier subsidiary company, GEM (Jingmen) Nickel-Cobalt Materials Co., Ltd., with registered capital of 500,000 yuan and 100% shareholding. This new company will be incorporated into the scope of consolidation in the current period.
4. ② In April 2022, second-tier subsidiary company GEM (Jiangsu) Cobalt Industry Co., Ltd. merged Taixing  Xinxin  Resources  and  Renewable  Utilization  Co.,  LTD.,  with  registered  capital  of 26,062,777.58 yuan and 100% shareholding, through equity acquisition that does not constitute business. This new company will be incorporated into the scope of consolidation in the current period.
5. ③ In October 2022, second-tier subsidiary company Fuan Qingmei Energy Materials Co., Ltd. set up  Ningde  Qingmei  Trading  Co.,  LTD.,  with  a  registered  capital  of  10  million  yuan  and  a shareholding of 60%. This new company will be incorporated into the scope of consolidation in the current period.
6. ④ In  December  2022,  the  company  established  GEM  (Shenzhen)  Super  Green  Technology Research Center Co., LTD., with a registered capital of 55 million yuan and 100% shareholding. This new company will be incorporated into the scope of consolidation in the current period.
- (2) Reduction of merge scope

In  November  2022,  the  company  cancelled  the  second-tier  subsidiary  company  Fengcheng Meisheng Renewable Resources Co., Ltd., and completed the industrial and commercial changes on November 10, 2022. After the disposal, the second-tier subsidiary company will no longer be included in the merger scope.

In  March  and April  2022,  the company signed capital increase and share increase agreements respectively. Upon completion of the capital increase, the Company holds 51.2159% of Green Tungsten Resource. The transaction resulted in an increase in capital reserves of RMB 5,182,479.96.

## X. RISK ASSOCIATED WITH FINANCIAL INSTRUMENTS

- (I) Risks associated with financial instruments

The Company's main financial instruments include equity investment, loans, accounts receivable, accounts payable, etc. Please refer to relevant items in Note V for a detailed description of each financial instrument. The risks associated with these financial instruments and the risk management policies  the  Company  has  in  place  to  mitigate  these  risks  are  described  below. The  Company's

management manages and monitors these exposures to ensure that these risks are controlled within the limits.

## 1. Market risk

Market risk of financial instruments refers to the risk  that the fair value or future cash flow of financial instruments will fluctuate due to changes in market prices, including exchange rate risk, interest rate risk and other price risks.

The Company adopts sensitivity analysis technology to analyze the possible impact of reasonable and possible changes of risk variables on current profit and loss or shareholders' equity. Since any risk variable rarely changes in isolation, and the correlations that exist between the variables will have  a  significant  effect  on  the  ultimate  amount  of  impact  of  a  change  in  a  risk  variable,  the following assumes that each variable changes independently.

## ① Exchange rate risk

Exchange rate risk refers to the risk that the fair value or future cash flow of financial instruments will  fluctuate  due  to  changes  in  foreign  exchange  rates.  The  Company's  exposure  to  foreign exchange risks is mainly related to US dollar, euro and Indonesian rupiah. Except for the purchase and sales of several subsidiaries of the Company in US dollar, euro and Indonesian rupiah, other major business activities of the Company are denominated and settled in Renminbi. Exchange rate risk has an impact on the Company's trading and overseas operating performance. As of December 31, 2022, the balance of the Company's foreign currency monetary items is referred to in Note VII, 61, "Foreign Currency Monetary Items".

The Company pays close attention to the impact of exchange rate changes on the Company's foreign exchange risk. In view of the risk of exchange rate fluctuations, the company actively carries out forward foreign exchange trading business, strengthens the study and analysis of exchange rate, timely adjusts the business strategy, and avoids exchange losses to the maximum extent.

## ② Interest rate risk

Interest rate risk refers to the risk that the fair value or future cash flow of financial instruments will fluctuate due to changes in market interest rates. The Company's interest rate risk arises from bank borrowings  and  interest-bearing  debt  such  as  bonds  payable.  Floating  interest  rate  financial liabilities  expose the Company to cash flow interest rate risk, while fixed interest rate financial liabilities expose the Company to fair value interest rate risk. The Company determines the relative ratio of fixed rate and floating rate contracts based on prevailing market conditions.

## 2. Credit risk

Credit risk refers to the risk that one party to a financial instrument fails to fulfill its obligations and causes financial losses to the other party.

At December 31, 2022, the Company's credit risk is primarily attributable to the financial assets recognized by the Company. The carrying amount of recognized financial assets in the consolidated balance sheet, and the maximum risk exposure is equal to the carrying value of these financial assets.

The Company's monetary funds are deposited in banks with high credit ratings, and the Company believes that there is no significant credit risk in them and that there will be almost no significant losses  resulting  from  bank defaults. In  addition,  for  notes  receivable, accounts receivable,  other receivables  and  receivables  financing,  the  Company  establishes  policies  to  control  credit  risk exposure. The Company evaluates the customer's credit qualification and sets the corresponding credit period based on the customer's financial condition, the possibility of obtaining guarantees from third parties, credit history and other factors such as current market conditions. The Company will regularly monitor the credit records of customers. For customers with poor credit records, the Company will use written reminders, shorten or cancel credit periods, etc., to ensure that the overall credit risk of the Company is within a controllable range. The Company has no material collateral and other credit enhancements due to debtors' mortgages.

The  Company's  method  of  assessing  whether  the  credit  risk  has  increased  since  the  initial recognition, the basis for determining the credit impairment of financial assets, the combination method of financial  instruments  for  assessing  the  expected  credit  risk  based  on  the  division  of portfolios,  and  the  policy  of  directly  writing  down  financial  instruments,  etc.,  are  listed  in  the accounting policies in the section of "Note V: Financial Assets Impairment".

## 3. Liquidity risk

Liquidity risk refers to the risk of capital shortage when an enterprise fulfills its obligation to settle by delivery of cash or other financial assets.

In managing liquidity risk, the Company maintains and monitors cash and cash equivalents deemed adequate by management to meet the Company's operating needs and mitigate the impact of cash flow fluctuations. Each subsidiary of the Company is responsible for its own cash flow forecast. On the  basis  of  summarizing the cash flow forecasts of its subsidiaries, the Company continuously monitors  the  short-term  and  long-term  funding  requirements  at  the  Group  level  to  ensure  that adequate cash reserves and marketable securities are maintained at any time; Continue to monitor compliance with borrowing agreements and obtain commitments from major financial institutions to provide sufficient stand-by funds to meet short-term and long-term funding requirements.

As of December 31, 2022, the Company's financial liabilities are listed as undiscounted contract cash flows by maturity date as follows:

Since there is no significant change in the operating environment, operating condition and financial condition of the invested enterprise, the

Company determines the fair value according to the cost method.

Forward settlement and sale valuation technology: Accrued fair value of forward foreign exchange settlement  contract  =  amount  of  foreign  currency  sold  *  (forward  exchange  rate  agreed  in  the contract - forward exchange rate at the end of the period similar to the delivery date of the forward foreign exchange settlement contract)/(1+ discount rate * Days from the balance sheet date to the delivery date /360), The accrued fair value of foreign exchange swap transaction = the amount of currency purchased at the near end of the contract * (the exchange rate at the far end of the contract -  the  forward  exchange  rate  at  the  end  of  the  period  similar  to  the  delivery  date  of  the  swap transaction) * the exchange rate of foreign currency to RMB on the balance sheet date/(1+ discount rate * the days from the balance sheet date to the delivery date /360); Accrued fair value of forex

put option contract = optionpremium income * Days from trading day to balance sheet date/days from trading day to delivery date.

(4) the fair value of financial assets and financial liabilities not measured at fair value Financial  assets  and  liabilities  not  measured  at  fair  value  mainly  include:  monetary  funds, receivables, short-term loans and payables.

The book value of the above financial assets and liabilities not measured at fair value differs little from fair value, so they are measured at amortized cost.

## XV. SUBSEQUENT EVENTS

## 1. Important non-adjustment matters

(1)  In  accordance  with  the  "Announcement  of  the  Memorandum  of  Understanding  on  the Construction  of  a  new-generation  Ultra-high  nickel  Multi-component  Precursor  Plant  and supporting nickel, cobalt and Manganese Raw Material System in Korea" issued by GEM Co., LTD. (the "Company") on March 25, in order to construct and operate a new-generation ultra-high nickel multi-component  precursor  (PCAM)  manufacturing  plant  for  secondary  power  batteries,  The Company, SK On Co., Ltd. (" SK On ") and ECOPRO MATERIALS Co., Ltd. (" ECOPRO ") have jointly signed a Memorandum of Understanding in Korea. Confirmed the Company's preliminary intention to establish and invest in a joint venture with SK On, ECOPRO or their affiliates on certain advanced  terms  in  the  Republic  of  Korea.  To  implement  the  MOU,  GEM  Korea  New  Energy Materials  Co.,  Ltd.  (GEM(Korea)),  a  subsidiary  of  the  company,  signed  a  Memorandum  of Understanding  (MOU)  with  Saemangeum  Development  Agency,  Gunsan  City,  North  Jeolla Province, and Korea Agriculture and Fishing Village Corporation for investment in a new secondary battery  precursor  plant.  In  a  joint  venture  with  SK  On,  ECOPRO  and  other  upstream  and downstream companies, the company will invest 1.21 trillion won (about RMB 6.4 billion) during 2023 to 2026 to build the first-stage ultra-high nickel multi-component precursor with an annual output of 43,000 tons and its supporting nickel, cobalt and manganese raw material system.

(2) According to the "Announcement on the Signing of the Memorandum of Understanding on the Construction of Battery Closed-loop Recycling Project with Mercedes-Benz China, Ningde Times and Bang" issued by GEM Co., LTD. (hereinafter referred to as the "Company") on February 28,The company, Mercedes-Benz (China) Automotive Sales Co., LTD., Beijing Benz Automotive Co., LTD. (hereinafter  collectively  referred  to  as  "Mercedes-Benz  China"),  Ningde  Times  New  Energy Technology Co., LTD. (hereinafter referred to as "Ningde Times") and Hunan Bang Pu Recycling Technology Co., LTD. (hereinafter referred to as "Bang Pu") jointly signed the Agreement on the Construction of Battery Closed-loop Recycling Project(hereinafter referred to as the "Memorandum of Understanding"), under which key raw materials such as nickel, cobalt, manganese and lithium recycled from Mercedes-Benz China's advanced recycling technology will be re-supplied to the supply chain and used in the production of new Mercedes-Benz batteries. All parties will carry out extensive and in-depth exploration and cooperation on battery recycling technology and recycling business model.

## 2. Explanation of profit distribution

On April 27, 2023, the fifteenth meeting of the sixth session of the board of directors of the company reviewed and approved the "Proposal on Profit Distribution in 2022". Based on the company's total share capital of 5,135,586,557.00 shares, a cash dividend will be distributed to all shareholders for every 10 shares [0.5] Yuan (tax included), 0 bonus shares (tax included) will be sent, and the share capital will not be converted from the accumulation fund.
